standard_text: The cultural diversity of India: languages, foods, clothes, festivals, dances, music and folk arts of different states; how customs change over time; unity in diversity (summary of NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 5).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 5 EVS worksheets for NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 5: dances, folk arts, foods, clothes, languages and harvest festivals of the states of India, and unity in diversity. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: India is one country with many cultures.
key_sub: Each state has its own dances, food and arts.
body_html:
How to think about it

India has 22 scheduled languages and many more spoken ones. Each region has its own food, clothes, festivals and arts, shaped by its weather and history. Bhangra is from Punjab, Garba from Gujarat and Bihu from Assam; Madhubani paintings come from Bihar and Warli art from Maharashtra; dhokla is a dish of Gujarat and puttu of Kerala.

Harvest festivals such as Pongal, Onam, Bihu and Baisakhi celebrate the crops. Customs change over time, for example eco-friendly clay idols and colours. Sharing each other's festivals and learning each other's languages keeps us united in diversity.

Example

Garba is a dance of…

Navratri

Answer: Gujarat

Example

Madhubani painting comes from…

Mithila region

Answer: Bihar

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all Indians eat the same food.
  • Mixing up Bihu (Assam) and Baisakhi (Punjab).
  • Thinking traditions never change.

faq.a: People of many languages, religions and customs living together peacefully as one nation.

faq.q: Why do clothes and food differ across India?
faq.a: Different regions have different weather, crops and traditions.
